newsitem.title: USA: Chevron shuts part of gasoline unit - source.
newsitem.headline: Chevron shuts part of gasoline unit - source.

text.p: Chevron Corp shut part of a gasoline-making unit at its Richmond, Calif., refinery over the weekend for planned maintenance scheduled to last a week, industry sources said Tuesday.
The shut equipment is part of the facility's 184,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) catalytic hydrotreater, a unit which turns heavier gas oils into gasolines and other light-end products.
A company spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
The shut unit is a minor part of overall gasoline production and will not disrupt customer shipments, an industry source said.
"There are other (Chevron) plants that will pick up the slack," the industry source said.
The Richmond refinery has a nameplate capacity of 225,000 bpd of crude oil, and makes roughly 100,000 bpd of gasoline.
Calfornia wholesale prices for gasoline rose about a cent a gallon early Tuesday in line with broader market gains.
